purpose: Test whether the known PROTEI DPI deployment at MegaCom/Alfa Telecom in Kyrgyzstan yields a censorship fingerprint that can be compared against Cuba/ETECSA and Russia/RDP-TSPU. Distinguish mechanism compatibility from vendor-unique attribution.

headline.content_filter_extension: CONFIRMED 2015-01/03 via Entensys UserGate Web Filter integrated with PROTEI DPI
headline.ooni_censorship_signal_2024: CONFIRMED AT COUNTRY/NETWORK-SET LEVEL; AS50223 INCLUDED

confirmed_megacom_stack.claim: PROTEI announced successful production deployment of its DPI platform in MegaCom's network; the platform was serving commercial traffic.
PROTEI and Entensys announced content filtering on MegaCom using PROTEI DPI plus UserGate Web Filter. Entensys classified requested sites and PROTEI DPI applied policy based on the response.

PROTEI technical documentation describes a traffic-processing architecture where an appliance/traffic filter handles packets and a control server inspects initial packets up to application layer, determines service/subscriber, obtains policy and instructs traffic handling.

ooni_kyrgyzstan_2024.aggregate_mechanism: Most OONI measurements showed TLS interference: session timeout after ClientHello during TLS handshake.
ooni_kyrgyzstan_2024.important_limit: The published finding reports the mechanism across five tested networks and does not, in the surfaced text, provide a raw per-AS packet trace proving that AS50223 specifically generated the exact same timeout behavior. Therefore AS50223-specific fingerprint is PARTIAL until raw per-AS measurements are extracted.

routing_confound.finding: Cloudflare's Q3 2024 disruption report identified AS12389 Rostelecom as MegaCom/AS50223's only upstream provider at the time of a September 2024 outage, and inferred damage on the MegaCom-Rostelecom connection.
routing_confound.implication: For 2024 path-level censorship measurements on AS50223, interference cannot be attributed to an on-net PROTEI device solely from the probe ASN. A policy-enforcement point upstream in Rostelecom, or another shared path element, must be excluded through hop/path localization.
routing_confound.current_state_note: Later routing data shows additional/changed upstream and peering relationships. The Cloudflare statement is used only for the 2024 temporal context.

CUBA_2017.mechanism: DPI reset connections to blocked HTTP sites and served blank block pages; Skype blocking showed injected TCP RST with low latency and inconsistent TTL, localizing injection to a nearby middlebox.

CUBA_2021.mechanism: During July 2021 protests, anomalous Signal measurements consistently failed TLS handshake with connection_reset; OONI assessed this as likely SNI-targeting DPI.

MEGACOM_2024.network: MegaCom / AS50223 included among affected networks
MEGACOM_2024.mechanism: TLS interference after ClientHello; published aggregate description emphasizes timeout, not a uniquely identified injected RST.

RUSSIA_RDP_TSPU_2024_2026.mechanism: OONI reports repeated centralized-style TLS interference in Russia: Discord/Viber commonly time out after first TLS write; Bluesky measurements show either TLS timeout or injected RST immediately after ClientHello; Telegram shows resets/timeouts on blocked endpoints.

fingerprint_assessment.shared_family: TLS/SNI-aware interference occurring immediately after or around ClientHello/first TLS write is compatible across MegaCom/Kyrgyzstan, Cuba, and Russia.
fingerprint_assessment.reason: Post-ClientHello timeout/reset is a generic DPI censorship technique observed in many unrelated countries and vendor environments, including Saudi Arabia and India. It cannot identify PROTEI or TSPU by itself.
fingerprint_assessment.cuba_vs_megacom: PARTIAL_MATCH at mechanism family level: Cuba 2021 connection_reset vs Kyrgyzstan 2024 mostly timeout after ClientHello. This is not a device fingerprint match.
fingerprint_assessment.megacom_vs_russia: PARTIAL_MATCH at mechanism family level: both show TLS interruption around ClientHello, but no packet-level uniqueness, TTL/IPID signature, injected-packet source behavior, or device metadata ties them together.
fingerprint_assessment.cuba_vs_russia: PARTIAL_MATCH at mechanism family level: both can produce RST near TLS ClientHello, but this behavior is non-unique and cannot establish shared implementation.

what_would_close_vendor_fingerprint: Raw AS50223 OONI measurements showing exact failure stage, reset/timeout type, remote/local endpoint behavior and timestamps.
Packet captures from MegaCom showing injected RST TTL, IPID, TCP sequence/ack patterns, directionality, timing and hop localization.
Comparable packet captures from Cuba/AS27725 and a confirmed PROTEI deployment other than MegaCom.
A PROTEI implementation or operations document specifying its block action for SNI/TLS targets (RST, drop/timeout, redirect) and packet construction behavior.
A matched alternate-path test on AS50223 that avoids Rostelecom while keeping the same destination, to distinguish MegaCom-local enforcement from upstream enforcement.
Device-management, procurement, support, or configuration evidence proving that the censorship function on AS50223 is executed by the installed PROTEI DPI rather than another box.
claim_ceiling: CONFIRMED: MegaCom/AS50223 deployed PROTEI DPI in 2014 and integrated PROTEI-based URL filtering in 2015.
CONFIRMED: AS50223 was one of five Kyrgyz networks in OONI's 2024 TikTok blocking finding; the dominant reported mechanism across measurements was post-ClientHello TLS timeout.
SUPPORTED: the observed Kyrgyz mechanism is technically compatible with capabilities expected of a DPI platform such as PROTEI.
NOT ESTABLISHED: the specific 2024 AS50223 block was executed by PROTEI DPI.
NOT ESTABLISHED: PROTEI has a vendor-unique RST/TLS fingerprint matching Cuba.
NOT ESTABLISHED: Cuba's measured DPI is PROTEI.
NOT ESTABLISHED: PROTEI and RDP/TSPU share code, packet-injection logic or a common control plane.
next_spider_step: Extract raw OONI measurements for AS50223 during 18-30 April 2024 and compare per-flow TLS failures against AS29061/AS47237 controls. The decisive question is whether AS50223 has a distinctive reset/timeout signature different from other Kyrgyz ISPs. If identical across unrelated networks, the national-policy/shared-upstream explanation gains weight; if AS50223 is uniquely different and matches a known PROTEI behavior, the vendor bridge strengthens.
